page.layout: Two woodcut medallions with captions at top, one on each side, with running head above; below them one column of text with two paragraphs; a small woodcut ornament at the foot, not text.

main_text.p: PHACEA, filius Romeliæ, tyrannide regnum Israël ob-tinuit, occiso Phacea filio Manahen, anno 5 2. Azariæ, siue Oziæ Regis Iudæ: qui erat annus mundi 3175. ante Christum natum 787. Hic quoque impius extitit, nec diuertit à peccatis Iero-boam filij Nabat. huius temporibus Theglat-Phalassar Assyrio-rum Rex, totam Galaaditen regionem oppressit, ac cepit, inco-las in Assyriam abduxit. Hoseas, siue Osee, tandem insidiis ag-gressus est hunc Phaceam, & interfecit eum, regnumque eius inuasit, cùm iam ille viginti regnasset annos. Vide lib. 4. Reg. 15. cap. & Ioseph. lib. 9. cap. 11.

HOSEA filius Ela, regnauit in Samaria super Israëlem post Phaceam quem occiderat, anno mundi 3195. ante Christum natum 767. anno septimo regni sui, Salmanazar Assyriorum Rex, Samariam obsedit, Hoseamque tributarium fecit. At verò Hoseas dum rebellat, tributáque Assyrio recusat, & dum à Sua Rege Ægypti auxilium petit, à Salmanazare obsessus est, qui vinctum misit in carcerem: Samariam cepit, Israëlitarum regnum perdidit, decémque tribus abduxit: transferens Israël in Assyrios. Itaque ab electione impij Ieroboam filij Nabat, ad quem, post mortem Salomonis, defecerant decem tribus ab Roboam filio Salomonis, afflixit Israëlem Dominus, & tradi-dit in manus diripientium, ob prævaricationes, præcipuè ob idololatriam. Consule librum 4. Regum cap. 17. & Ioseph. lib. 9. cap. 15.

page.notes: Two woodcut portrait medallions are not text; only their captions are transcribed. Spacing in the numbers 5 2, 3175, 787, 3195 and 767 is uncertain in the scan and is copied as read. The bottom ornament is a decorative woodcut and is omitted.
